newsitem.title: USA: Texaco a high flyer as oil prices surge.
newsitem.headline: Texaco a high flyer as oil prices surge.

text.p: Texaco Inc led energy stocks higher on Monday as oil prices surged, cresting to a new post-Gulf War high in London this morning.
Texaco shares hit a new 52-week high of 101-1/4 in early trading before settling back to 100-7/8, up 2-3/4 at midday.
Analysts said surging crude prices were boosting the entire sector. In London, IPE Brent crude futures rose to a new post-Gulf War high of $24.75 a barrel.
Exxon Corp shares rose 1-3/8 to 37-3/4, and Chevron Corp rose 3/4 to 66-1/2, after hitting a new 52-week high of 66-5/8.

"Texaco is a more leveraged crude play," said analyst James Falvey at Smith Barney in Boston. He said several other factors had combined to boost Texaco's share price: "The (stock) market is doing well, there's some continued momentum after last week's announcement, and there's some sector rotation going on, people had been underweighted in the oil sector".
Last week, Texaco and Shell Oil Co confirmed they are discussing what could be the largest downstream oil merger in U.S. history.
Falvey also noted that Texaco would be reporting third quarter earnings soon and said they "should look better with their chemical operations off the sheet."
"The chemical cycle was just at a horrendous point and the chemical operations earnings had languished," he said.
NYMEX heating oil prices also surged, helped by news of an Ohio refinery problem and news of renewed intra-Kurdish tensions in northern Iraq, traders said.
